reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with NormedAddCommGroup,InnerProductSpace R,FiniteDimensional R,MeasurableSpace and BorelSpace instances and canonical full-space volume,including dimension zero. Let W:E->R be C2 and assume exp(-W) is volume-integrable and its volume integral strictly positive. Let m,M:R satisfy m>0,m<=M. Assume for EVERY x,a:E BOTH bounds
  m*||a||^2 <= (fderiv R (fderiv R W) x a) a,
  (fderiv R (fderiv R W) x a) a <= M*||a||^2.
Define mu=volume.tilted(x->-W(x)),the actual normalized exp(-W)/positive partition Gibbs measure.
For EVERY actual real function f:E->R,assume f C1,actual MemLp f 2 mu,and actual MemLp (gradient f) 2 mu. No compact support or mean-zero condition is required of f;these are genuine scalar/vector AE strong-measurability and finite-L2 hypotheses,not inferred from finite probability alone.
Then ALL of the following actual integrability assertions hold:
  Integrable f mu,
  Integrable (x->(f(x)-integral f(y) dmu(y))^2) mu,
  Integrable (x->||gradient(f)(x)||^2) mu.
These three and only these conjuncts are the approved Admissible(mu,f) predicate. Moreover,
  m*integral (f(x)-integral f(y) dmu(y))^2 dmu(x)
  <= integral ||gradient(f)(x)||^2 dmu(x).
The left integral is exactly variance(mu,f);the right is exactly dirichletEnergy(mu,f),with NO extra prefactor. All integrals use the SAME actual mu,including the inner mean;there is no division by mass in the API's mean formula (mu here is normalized). The gradient is exactly (InnerProductSpace.toDual R E).symm(fderiv R f x),the genuine real Riesz representative,with actual C1 derivatives ensured by the input.
This statement has no D parameter or graph/domain premise;the operator mentioned in background context is not added as a theorem assumption. Both lower and upper global C2 curvature controls,integrability and positive partition remain explicit. Admissible and the inequality are outputs,not supplied certificates. The result applies to every C1 scalar-and-gradient L2 function,not just already-centered or compact functions. No rough Hessian,Hessian-inverse anisotropic inequality,normalized-score differentiation,marginal-law inequality,measurable selector or main/expected-cost composition is asserted.
objects: C2 W,real m/M,positive integrable partition,actual normalized Gibbs mu;EVERY actual C1 real f with scalar/vector-gradient weighted L2;literal Admissible three integrability outputs,actual centered-square variance and gradient-square Dirichlet integral.
domains: Displayed finite-dimensional real inner-product/Borel fullspace E including0,volume. Scalar f:E->R,genuine Riesz gradient:E->E. All f/gradient MemLp and all inner-mean/variance/energy integrals use SAME actual mu. Admissible exactly Integrable f,Integrable centered-square,Integrable gradient-norm-square;no built-in smoothness conjunct. API energy no prefactor,API mean integral no mass division.
quantifiers: Universal E,W,m,M satisfying all explicit premises;Hessian lower/upper forall x,a;let mu;forall f:E->R,C1 -> actual scalar MemLp2 -> actual gradient MemLp2 -> Admissible and m*variance<=dirichletEnergy. No D binder/domain/centered or compact input requirement.
assumptions: W C2,Integrable exp(-W) volume,strictly positive partition;m>0,m<=M;all-point all-vector actual nested-fderiv lower/upper quadratic bounds;f C1,MemLp f2mu and MemLp gradient f2mu. BOTH curvature controls retained,no assumed Poincare/coercivity/limit certificate,no automatic unbounded-L2-from-probability shortcut.
conclusion: For every such f,all three actual integrabilities f/centered-square/gradient-square and m*integral(f-mean_mu f)^2 dmu<=integral||gradient f||^2 dmu. Genuine explicit Admissible/variance/Dirichlet APIs fully expanded with no extra prefactor.
scopes: Input f arbitrary not already-centered or compact. Predicate output no hidden extra smoothness condition;actual derivatives ensured by C1 assumption. Original D proof context not an added premise. Both C2 m/M controls explicit,not lower-only. No rough Hessian,anisotropic/marginal/normalized-score/main/cost conclusion or selector.
